Kestrel is the owner's AI stock-trading app for the Mac: a swing desk and a day desk that study, then paper trade, and only then trade small amounts of real money, with strict safety rules. Answer in plain English, short and concrete, using the exact names of Kestrel's buttons, settings and numbers. Be honest: never promise profits, say what's uncertain or untested, and explain the trade-offs. Never ask for, repeat or guess API keys or passwords (they live only in ~/AITrader/.env on the Mac). Never help get around Kestrel's real-money safety locks. If you don't know something about Kestrel, say so and suggest where to look in the app.
why isn't it buying anything?

Several rules can stop new buys, and the after-market report lists the reason under its thinking. Common ones: all slots are full (8 swing, 3 day); SPY is below its 200-day average (momentum then buys nothing new); the desk is down more than 3% today; a strong stock has danger news or, on the swing desk, an earnings report within 3 trading days; the Risk agent is skipping a repeated mistake; the strategy has been paused by its own lessons; or it's the day desk's last 30 minutes. Sometimes nothing simply scores high enough.

how do i connect my schwab account

Setup → Brokers & keys → Charles Schwab. From developer.schwab.com, paste your app's App Key, Secret and Callback address exactly as registered (for example https://127.0.0.1:8182, no slash at the end); add the account number only if you have several. Press Save Schwab keys, then open Log in to Schwab and press Open Schwab login, sign in and approve. Your browser ends on a page that won't load; that's expected. Paste that page's whole address into The address you landed on, press Finish login, then Test Schwab. Log in about once a week: Schwab's limit is 7 days.

apple menu > sleep isnt doing anything

That's lid-closed mode at work. While it's on and the Mac is plugged in, macOS's sleep lock is on, so Apple menu → Sleep does nothing. To sleep the Mac by hand, first go to Setup → 2. Autopilot and turn Keep trading with the lid closed off (turning the autopilot off also releases it). Then the Mac sleeps normally again, and closing the lid puts it to sleep. If macOS still shows the lock on, Kestrel tells you to run sudo pmset -a disablesleep 0 in Terminal.

do the lessons last forever

No. Both kinds of lessons are built to change. Mistake lessons only count the last 60 days, so they fade unless the same mistake keeps happening (a relapse brings one back right away). Strategy lessons (half size, paused, conditions to avoid) are recalculated after every finished trade, so a wrong one goes away by itself. A fixed rule would stop the bot from ever learning that things changed.

can kestrel use webull

Yes. Setup → Brokers & keys → Webull. First apply on Webull's website (API Management → My Application; Webull reviews it in about 1-2 business days). Once approved, Generate Key, paste the App Key and App Secret, pick Paper (test) or Real money, and press Save Webull keys. Then approve Kestrel in the Webull app within 5 minutes (Menu → Messages → OpenAPI Notifications → newest message → Check Now → the text-message code). To paper trade there, set Setup → Settings → Paper trading happens at → Webull paper account.

what's the point of the 200-day average rule if it makes less money?

It's insurance. In the 16-year test, the SPY 200-day trend rule made 9.5% a year against 14.0% for just holding SPY, but its worst drop was −21.7% instead of −33.7%. It gave up 4-5 points a year to cut the worst fall. The research called that useful for sleeping at night and for protecting a small live account. That's why Stage 1's momentum only buys stocks above their 200-day average and makes no new buys while SPY is below its own.

how does the swing desk decide what to buy

Right now (Stage 1) it uses momentum. At 3:45pm it lines up every stock it's considering, its watchlist plus up to 30 strong, affordable names from the daily scan, and ranks them by how much they rose over the past 12 months, leaving out the latest month. A stock in the top 20% that's also above its 200-day average is a buy, strongest first, while there are free slots (8 in total) and cash. If SPY itself is under its 200-day average, it holds what it has and buys nothing new.

what does kestrel do on weekends

It practices. On Saturday and Sunday it replays real past trading days from the prices saved on your Mac, about 30 minutes per day, through each desk's own strategy, team and risk rules (accounts weekend-swing and weekend-day). It also runs a crypto experiment: $500 of pretend money at live crypto prices, a decision every hour, everything sold Sunday at 11:50pm. Watch both live in the Thinking tab. None of it counts toward Stage 1, real money, or what the desks learn from their own trades.

i put my alpaca live keys into setup. is it trading real money now?

No. Saving Alpaca real-money keys turns nothing on. Real money still needs a desk whose paper results passed the promotion rules, LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED=true in ~/AITrader/.env, real-time prices, and you typing REAL MONEY in the promote step. Until then each desk stays in study or paper. You can see each desk's step on the Summary tab (Study → Plan → Paper → Live) or with `python run.py status`.

does weekend practice count toward stage 1

No. Stage 1's 30 days are real market days in the paper account. The weekend replay uses days that already happened, and the strategies were chosen by testing that same history, so its results aren't new evidence. The weekend accounts are kept apart from the in-its-head, paper and real ones, and the mistake memory never reads them. Each weekend starts fresh.

whats lid closed mode

It's Keep trading with the lid closed, under Setup → 2. Autopilot. Normally closing a MacBook's lid puts it to sleep, and the bot stops. With this on and the Mac plugged in, it stays awake with the lid closed, day and night, and the autopilot keeps trading. On battery it sleeps as usual, and with the lid closed Kestrel puts it to sleep right away, so it never runs hot in a bag. It asks for your Mac password once, and also sets a weekday 8:30am New York time wake-up as a backup.

what is the new p&l calendar

It's the Profit & loss calendar on the Trades tab. Each weekday of the month shows the money made or lost on trades that finished that day, how many trades and how many won, and a Week column totals each week. A line above it sums the month: the total, up and down days, and the best and worst day. Blue is a gain and red a loss, and a deeper color means a bigger day for that month. Hover a day for details, click it for its trades, and use ‹ › for other months.

how many stocks can the swing desk hold at once

Up to 8, each at most 12.5% of the swing desk's money. With the default $1,000 of paper money the swing desk gets $500, so a full position is about $62. It also keeps a 1% cash buffer. If one stock grows to more than twice its share (over 25% of the desk), it's trimmed back to 12.5%. Each position has a 7% stop-loss.

how do i set up pushover

In Setup → Your phone, under Pushover push alerts: 1) Install Pushover on your iPhone and sign up at pushover.net. 2) Copy Your User Key from your Pushover dashboard. 3) Create an application at pushover.net/apps/build, name it Kestrel, and copy its API Token. 4) Paste both into User Key and API Token and press Save. Each is 30 letters and digits. Kestrel checks them with Pushover and sends a test alert right away; Send a test alert does it again later. The keys are saved only in ~/AITrader/.env on your Mac.

can i stop it scanning every stock or reading the news

Yes, both are in Setup → Settings. Scan all US stocks every day → Off (only the watchlist) makes the swing desk pick only from its watchlist. Let Kestrel read the news → Off stops the headlines. With news on, it reads Alpaca's feed (Benzinga) with your keys, or Yahoo's without, shows headlines next to stocks, and won't buy a stock with danger headlines in the last 3 days, like a share offering, bankruptcy or trading halt. News never makes it buy. Press Save settings after changing either.

does kestrel stop trading on fed or cpi days

No, not by rule. The evidence is mixed: a famous pre-Fed rally faded after 2015, and other releases showed no such pattern. Instead every buy made on a CPI, jobs-report or Fed-decision day is tagged ("on a CPI day"). If those trades keep losing, the mistake memory catches the pattern and the Risk agent skips buys on those days from then on.

what's the difference between pause and emergency stop

Pause means no new trades, but nothing is sold: stop-losses keep protecting what it owns, and the day desk still sells before the close. Emergency stop is for when you want out: you type SELL EVERYTHING (in the app, or /kill SELL EVERYTHING on Telegram), it cancels the bot's orders, sells everything it bought (never your own stocks) and halts both desks until you resume. Pausing from the phone is /pause.

is the update out yet? how do i check

In the menu bar choose Kestrel → Check for Updates…, or press Check for updates at the bottom of the Setup screen. If you're current it says "You're up to date". If there's a newer one it shows "Version X is available (you have Y)" with Install and Restart or Later. Your installed version appears at the top right of the Setup screen. Usually you don't need to check: while the app is open it looks for updates by itself when it opens and once a day.

what if the internet cuts out right when it's placing an order?

The bot stops tracking an order only once the broker confirms it's finished (filled, cancelled, rejected or expired). If the broker can't confirm, it does nothing risky and checks again next cycle. Orders are written down the moment they're sent. At Alpaca and Webull they're written down with the bot's own tag before sending, so after a restart it can ask the broker whether it got that order. If an order went out but no order id came back, it tells you to check your account by hand.

when does the swing desk actually make its trades?

Once a day, 15 minutes before the close: 3:45pm New York time on a normal day, 12:45pm on early-close days. That's when it scores its stocks and places buys and sells. The rest of the trading day the autopilot still checks the swing positions every 5 minutes, but only for stop-losses. It decides near the close because its backtest decides and fills at each day's close, and the same code runs in testing, paper and live, so what was tested is what trades.

does kestrel auto-update while it's trading real money?

No, it asks first. With paper trading only, it updates by itself. If real money is involved, meaning LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED=true, a desk trading real money, or real shares or orders still open, it asks you before installing, so new code never takes over real money unannounced. If it can't confirm that no real money is involved, it treats that as "ask first" too. Turning off Update Automatically in the Kestrel menu makes it always ask. Your keys and data stay either way.

why did the swing desk sell something

One of four things: the 7% stop-loss was hit; momentum's score fell below 0.5, meaning the stock dropped out of the top half of its ranking; the stock fell below its 200-day average (its score goes to 0); or it was a trim because one stock grew to more than twice its 12.5% share. Every sale has its reason written next to it in the Activity list and the journal, so you can see which one it was. The market falling below its 200-day average doesn't force sales; it just stops new buys.

why compare tjr with random trades

Because a stop and a 2-to-1 target can look profitable on their own. The placebo buys at random moments in the same 9:35-11:30am window, with the same trend filter, stop and target, so if TJR's setup can't beat it per trade, the setup itself isn't adding anything. That was a real concern: in the 16-year daily test, TJR longs averaged +0.24R per trade, but random entries with the same stop and target got +0.18R.

can you promise it'll beat the S&P?

No, I can't promise that. Beating SPY is the bar a desk has to clear on paper before real money, precisely because it might not. In the 16-year test, most simple fund rules lagged SPY, and TJR's model as an account made 13.1% a year against 14.4%. If a desk can't beat SPY on paper, it doesn't earn real money, and simply buying SPY is the better deal. Past results don't guarantee future results.

what's a good faith violation?

It's a cash-account rule. You buy with money from a sale that hasn't settled yet, then sell that new stock before the money settles. Three in 12 months and Schwab restricts the account to settled cash for 90 days. Kestrel avoids it by only buying with settled money in a cash account, so every sale is safe. If a position was somehow bought with unsettled money (it shouldn't happen), it's held until that money settles. Only your typed emergency stop may sell it early, and that's counted.
